altText: Scientific cutaway of a cannabis seed labeling the seed coat, cotyledon tissue, embryo axis, radicle, and micropyle.
productionBrief: Academic studio botanical plate. Single mature cannabis seed shown intact beside a precise cutaway. Label seed coat, cotyledon tissue, embryo axis, radicle, and micropyle. Neutral cream-to-charcoal background, realistic botanical texture, clean leader lines, no decorative cannabis imagery, no yellow cast, no exaggerated embryo anatomy.

altText: Cannabis root-zone cutaway showing the main root axis, lateral roots, fine absorbing roots, root hairs, and occupied substrate volume.
productionBrief: High-detail academic root-zone cutaway of a healthy cannabis plant in an inert generic substrate profile. Clearly distinguish primary axis, lateral roots, fine roots and root-hair zone. Show realistic branching density without implying every root is visibly white. Include scale context and labeled callouts. No nutrient-brand imagery and no decorative yellow grading.

altText: Healthy cannabis fan leaf reference plate showing leaflet shape, serrations, venation, midrib, petiole, upper surface, and lower surface.
productionBrief: Academic studio reference plate of a healthy mature cannabis fan leaf. Include top and underside views plus detail callouts for leaflet, serration, midrib, secondary veins and petiole. Natural healthy green variation, realistic texture, calibrated neutral lighting, no glossy artificial look, no yellow filter.

altText: Female cannabis flower anatomy plate labeling bracts, stigmas, pistillate structures, sugar leaves, and clustered floral tissue.
productionBrief: High-resolution botanical anatomy plate of a female cannabis inflorescence using a realistic representative flower cluster. Label bracts, paired stigmas emerging from pistillate flowers, sugar leaves and clustered floral structure. Avoid calling the whole bract a calyx. Do not invent visible ovaries or exaggerated resin. Neutral studio lighting and scientifically restrained labeling.

altText: Microscope comparison of bulbous, capitate-sessile, and capitate-stalked glandular cannabis trichomes with relative scale.
productionBrief: Scientific microscope-style comparison plate of glandular cannabis trichome types: bulbous, capitate-sessile and capitate-stalked. Show relative scale and morphology without presenting them as equal size. Include stalk and gland-head labels where applicable. Realistic translucent tissue and resin appearance, neutral color balance, no psychedelic styling.

altText: Interactive root-hair absorption diagram connecting water films, root hairs, selective membrane transport, oxygen availability, and inward movement toward xylem.
productionBrief: Academic process diagram showing a fine root with root hairs in a generic substrate pore network. Connect water films, dissolved ions, root-zone oxygen, membrane transport and movement toward xylem. Avoid depicting nutrients as freely passing through membranes or implying root hairs are permanent structures.

altText: Interactive xylem transport diagram showing root uptake, a continuous water column, cohesion, transpiration pull, and delivery to shoots.
productionBrief: Whole-plant transport diagram emphasizing xylem from roots through stem to leaves. Show root uptake, conduit continuity, cohesion-tension context, transpiration-driven pull and shoot delivery. Do not depict xylem as an active pump.

altText: Interactive stomatal diagram showing guard cells, an open pore, carbon dioxide entry, water-vapor exit, and temperature-humidity vapor-pressure context.
productionBrief: Scientific leaf-surface diagram centered on a stomatal complex. Show paired guard cells, pore, CO2 diffusion inward and water-vapor diffusion outward. Explain that guard-cell regulation is physiological and that temperature plus humidity shape vapor-pressure conditions.

altText: Interactive structural sequence from flower initiation through cluster expansion, bract expansion, resin development, and maturation.
productionBrief: Development sequence based on visible structural progression rather than fixed week numbers. Show initiation, cluster expansion, bract expansion, increasing glandular coverage, and maturation. Keep cultivar variability explicit and avoid using stigma color alone as a maturity endpoint.

altText: Interactive cutaway of a capitate-stalked cannabis trichome showing the stalk, secretory disc, subcuticular storage space, cuticle, and epidermal surface.
productionBrief: Simplified academic cutaway of a capitate-stalked glandular trichome. Label multicellular stalk, secretory disc cells, subcuticular storage cavity, cuticle and epidermal origin. Preserve the distinction between secretory tissue and stored resin.

altText: Interactive seed imbibition sequence showing a dry cannabis seed taking up water, swelling, restarting metabolism, and approaching radicle emergence.
productionBrief: Academic germination sequence showing hydration before visible radicle emergence. Distinguish dry seed, water uptake, seed-coat hydration, tissue swelling, metabolic restart, and subsequent radicle emergence. Do not imply imbibition guarantees viability or completed germination.

altText: Interactive apical-dominance diagram comparing an intact shoot apex with lateral bud response after apex removal.
productionBrief: Botanical architecture diagram comparing an intact dominant shoot apex with a topped plant. Show axillary buds, changed branch growth and a restrained hormone-signaling context. Avoid presenting auxin as a single direct off-switch for lateral buds; note interaction with other hormonal and resource signals.

altText: Interactive leaf photosynthesis diagram connecting light capture, carbon dioxide entry, water supply, chloroplast function, and carbohydrate production.
productionBrief: Academic leaf-level process diagram showing usable light reaching the leaf, CO2 diffusing through stomata, xylem water supply, chloroplast-scale photosynthetic activity and carbohydrate output. Avoid implying that photosynthesis is controlled by light alone or that all fixed carbon immediately becomes glucose exported from the leaf.

altText: Interactive leaf symptom vocabulary comparing chlorosis, necrosis, spotting, curl or distortion, and symptom location patterns.
productionBrief: Diagnostic vocabulary plate using representative cannabis leaves. Compare chlorosis, necrosis, spotting or lesions, curl or distortion, and old-versus-new or upper-versus-lower location. This is descriptive training, not a nutrient-deficiency identification chart; avoid mapping any single pattern to one diagnosis.

altText: Interactive seed-development sequence from pollination and fertilization through embryo development, seed-coat differentiation, and physical maturity.
productionBrief: Botanical reproductive sequence connecting compatible pollination to fertilization, embryo development, maternal seed-coat differentiation, filling and physical maturity. Keep pollen contact distinct from successful fertilization and avoid implying mature external appearance guarantees seed viability.

altText: Interactive whole-plant VPD diagram connecting leaf vapor pressure, ambient air vapor pressure, the vapor-pressure gradient, stomatal response, transpiration, and root water supply.
productionBrief: Whole-plant VPD process visual. Show leaf vapor pressure as temperature-dependent and near saturation inside healthy leaf air spaces, ambient vapor pressure from temperature and RH, the resulting gradient, stomatal regulation, transpiration and root/xylem water supply. Avoid fixed universal VPD targets and avoid treating VPD as the sole control of transpiration.

altText: Interactive rhizosphere map showing the root surface, root exudates, microbial communities, water and dissolved ions, and oxygen conditions in the root-influenced zone.
productionBrief: Academic rhizosphere cross-section around a living fine root. Show a narrow root-influenced zone with water films, dissolved ions, root exudates, representative bacteria and fungi, and oxygen diffusion. Avoid portraying all microbes as beneficial or the rhizosphere as a uniform fixed layer.

altText: Interactive phloem transport map showing a source leaf, regulated loading, sieve transport pathways, growing sinks, and source-dependent transport direction.
productionBrief: Whole-plant source-to-sink phloem diagram. Identify source leaves, loading into phloem, sieve elements and representative sinks such as growing shoots, roots, flowers or seeds. Emphasize that different pathways can carry assimilates in different directions and avoid depicting phloem as a passive gravity-driven downward pipe.

altText: Interactive pollen pathway showing production in staminate anthers, release and transport, stigma contact, pollen-tube growth, and fertilization context.
productionBrief: Botanical reproductive process diagram separating pollen production, release or transport, compatible stigma contact, pollen germination, pollen-tube growth and fertilization. Keep pollination distinct from successful fertilization and do not imply every pollen grain reaching a stigma produces a seed.

altText: Interactive canopy PPFD map showing the light source, a measurement grid, high-light zones, shaded zones, and spatial uniformity across the canopy.
productionBrief: Top-and-side canopy lighting diagram with an explicit PPFD measurement grid. Show fixture geometry, canopy surface, high and low zones, leaf overlap and spatial uniformity. Use relative or example values rather than universal intensity prescriptions, and make clear that one center measurement cannot represent the full canopy.

altText: Interactive trichome sampling map comparing flower bracts and sugar leaves, multiple flower sites, standardized optics, and repeated observations over time.
productionBrief: Microscope sampling guide showing representative flower bracts versus surrounding sugar leaves, several canopy sampling locations, consistent magnification and lighting, and repeat observation over time. Avoid presenting sugar-leaf trichomes as interchangeable with bract trichomes for floral maturity assessment.

altText: Interactive diagnostic workflow progressing from precise observation to context collection, ranked hypotheses, discriminating checks, and evidence-based updates.
productionBrief: Diagnostic decision map beginning with symptom description, then environmental and root-zone context, a ranked differential across environmental, root-zone, nutritional, pest, pathogen and physical causes, a discriminating measurement or inspection, and iterative updating. Do not collapse the workflow into one-image diagnosis.
